chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not recite in the obligatory prayer with less than one Chapter, nor with more.'

key_terms.الْمَكْتُوبَةِ: The obligatory (fixed) prayer, specifically referring to the Fajr prayer or the general obligatory prayers where recitation is prescribed.

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum and maximum amount of Quran to recite in the obligatory prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential boundaries for the 'written' (Fatiha) recitation in obligatory prayers, specifying that it must consist of exactly one Surah—neither less nor more. In Shia fiqh, this is often interpreted to mean that while the Fatiha is mandatory, adding another Surah is permissible but not required to fulfill the specific obligation of the 'written' portion, thus preventing both deficiency and unnecessary prolixity in the core recitation.
